chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated from Umar ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Ishaq ibn Ammar as-Sayrafi, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:

For the Qa'im (the Rising One) there are two occultations: one is long, and the other is short. In the first, only a special group of his Shia knows his location, and in the second, no one knows his location except the special guardians of his religion.
ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of the Imam al-Qa'im according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological framework for the Twelver Shia doctrine of the two occultations, distinguishing between the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*) and the Major Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Kubra*). It highlights the gradual transition of authority, where knowledge of the Imam's location narrows from the exclusive circle of the Four Deputies to the broader community, underscoring the period of waiting (*Intizar*) as a time of spiritual testing and preservation of the Imam's hidden presence.
